page.overview:
What is Legendary Pokémon?

A Legendary Pokémon is a unique type of Pokémon that is renowned for its exceptional power and rarity, making them the most coveted type of Pokémon for Pokémon Trainers to obtain. In the core series, Legendary Pokémon tend to have a lower catch rate than other Pokémon, so players are often advised to use a Master Ball when trying to catch one.

Legendary Pokémon are usually the version mascots of a game in the core series, starting with Ho-Oh and Lugia with respectively or Zamazenta from Pokemon Shield and Zacian in Pokemon Sword for some examples. In various paired games, the Legendary Pokémon is exclusive to the respective games, and can be obtained in the other game only through trading; this practice began with , where Groudon can be encountered in the former game and Kyogre in the latter game.

A few Legendary Pokémon have alternate forms that it can change into. The first Legendary Pokémon that was given one is Giratina, which was given an Altered Forme in . Certain Legendary Pokémon such as Terapagos can only become their alternate form in battle. Kyurem, Necrozma, and Calyrex can achieve their alternative forms with a different Pokémon.

By Generation VIII, the three Legendary Birds—Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres—became the first Legendary Pokémon to receive regional forms, specifically in Galar.
